# MatchClaimField { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField(
    raw=None,
    *,
    source_fields=None,
    name=None,
    metadata=None,
)
```

A ``SemanticField[MatchClaim]`` columnar store for pairwise claims.

``MatchClaimField`` is the Field paired with the :class:`MatchClaim`
scalar.  It holds a large set of synchronous pairwise alignment
claims (millions of rows) in a single derived struct column instead of one
frozen :class:`MatchClaim` per claim.  Individual claims are materialised
lazily, only when a row is indexed or iterated.

Like every paired Field, its struct schema is derived from the scalar by
:func:`~timetoalign.core.fields.derive_arrow_struct` — so the inner column
type is exactly ``MatchClaimField.pa_schema``.  Shared provenance is held
once at field level as a single :class:`MatchMetadata` (or ``None``) and
**injected on read**, mirroring how
:class:`~timetoalign.core.time.CoordinateField` carries its ``unit``
outside the data: the struct column's ``metadata`` sub-field is left null
in bulk, and :meth:`__getitem__` injects the field-level metadata into each
materialised :class:`MatchClaim`.  This keeps the store compact (one struct
column, no per-row metadata) while remaining a genuine SemanticField.

Every row represents a synchronous claim with a start anchor and an
optional end anchor. NOMATCH claims remain outside this store because
they carry no coordinate pair to query.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name     | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                  |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| table    | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`)                              | The backing single-column :class:`pyarrow.Table` (read-only property) whose one column is the derived ``MatchClaim`` struct. |
| metadata | [MatchMetadata](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchMetadata`) \| None | Shared :class:`MatchMetadata` (or ``None``) applied to every materialised claim.                                             |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> agent = Agent(name="dtw", type=AgentType.software, identifier="v1")
>>> meta = MatchMetadata(agent=agent)
>>> field = MatchClaimField.from_columns(
...     timeline_a_ids=["A", "A", "B"],
...     timeline_b_ids=["B", "C", "C"],
...     coordinate_a=[0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
...     coordinate_b=[10.0, 20.0, 21.0],
...     unit_a=TimeUnit.quarters,
...     unit_b=TimeUnit.seconds,
...     metadata=meta,
... )
>>> len(field)
3
>>> field[0].timeline_a_id, field[0].timeline_b_id
('A', 'B')
```

### at { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.at }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.at(timeline_id, coordinate)
```

Return claims relevant at ``(timeline_id, coordinate)``.

The selection is a vectorized PyArrow boolean mask over the struct
column. Instant rows compare their start coordinate exactly. Interval
rows use closed containment between their start and end coordinates.
No claim is materialised and the rest of the field is never touched;
the shared metadata carries over.

Coordinate matching is exact in the query coordinate's declared
number representation. There is no tolerance or nearest-value
fallback.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                | Description                                   | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`)                                        | The timeline the queried coordinate lives on. | _required_ |
| coordinate  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | A raw or typed coordinate on that timeline.   | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                   |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField` holding only the matching rows |
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | (possibly empty).                                             |

|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField` holding only the matching rows. |

### connects_groups { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.connects_groups }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.connects_groups(group_a_ids, group_b_ids)
```

Whether any claim spans the two given sets of timeline ids.

True when at least one row has one side in ``group_a_ids`` and the
other side in ``group_b_ids``.  The test is a vectorized mask reduced
with :func:`pyarrow.compute.any`; no claim is materialised, so it
answers commensurability over a million-row field in one pass.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                         | Description                     | Default    |
|-------------|------------------------------|---------------------------------|------------|
| group_a_ids | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] | Timeline ids on one side.       | _required_ |
| group_b_ids | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] | Timeline ids on the other side. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type           | Description                               |
|--------|----------------|-------------------------------------------|
|        | [bool](`bool`) | True if some claim connects the two sets. |

### coordinate_pairs { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.coordinate_pairs }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.coordinate_pairs()
```

Read the four defining columns in bulk, materialising no claim.

This is the read a tabular consumer wants: the two timeline ids and
the two anchor coordinates of every row, as four parallel Python
lists pulled straight off the Arrow columns.  Materialising the rows
as :class:`MatchClaim` objects instead costs orders of magnitude more
for the same information.

Each coordinate is read in the representation its own ``unit``
declares, so an anchor authored at ``5/3`` quarters comes back as
``Fraction(5, 3)`` rather than as the double nearest to it.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                                         |
|--------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[str](`str`)\] | ``(timeline_a_ids, timeline_b_ids, coordinates_a, coordinates_b)``, |
|        | [list](`list`)\[[str](`str`)\] | all of length ``len(self)``.                                        |

### filter { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.filter }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.filter(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    between=None,
    within=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
)
```

Return a filtered view following the unified filter API.

Every criterion is a vectorized boolean mask over the struct column;
no claim is materialised and the shared metadata carries over.  All
non-default criteria are combined with logical AND.

``include_domains`` / ``include_units`` are deliberately absent: they
need per-timeline metadata (domain, unit) that this store does not
hold.  A caller that owns that metadata — an
:class:`~timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle`, say — resolves
them into the set of timeline ids that pass and hands that set to
``within``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                   | Description                                                                                                      | Default   |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| timeline_id      | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Keep rows involving this exact id on either side (equivalent to :meth:`connecting`).                             | `None`    |
| timeline_ids     | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                   | Keep rows involving **any** id in this set on either side.                                                       | `None`    |
| id_pattern       | [str](`str`) \| None                                   | Keep rows involving any id matching this regex (``re.search`` against the field's :attr:`timeline_ids`).         | `None`    |
| between          | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[str](`str`), [str](`str`)\] \| None | Keep rows connecting exactly these two ids (order-independent).                                                  | `None`    |
| within           | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                   | Keep rows whose **both** ids are in this set.  This is the primitive behind domain- and unit-restricted queries. | `None`    |
| synchronous_only | [bool](`bool`)                                         | A no-op — every row in this store is a synchronous claim by class invariant.                                     | `False`   |
| nomatch_only     | [bool](`bool`)                                         | Returns an **empty** field, for the same reason.                                                                 | `False`   |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                                                      |
|--------|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`.  With no criteria set, a copy of |
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | the whole field is returned.                                     |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If ``synchronous_only`` and ``nomatch_only`` are both set. |

### from_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_claims }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_claims(claims, *, metadata=None)
```

Build a field from existing :class:`MatchClaim` objects.

Every claim must be synchronous and carry a start anchor. Interval
claims retain their end anchors.

If ``metadata`` is ``None`` and all claims share one identical
:class:`MatchMetadata` (by equality), that metadata is adopted as the
field-level provenance; otherwise the field's metadata stays ``None``
(no per-row metadata is ever stored).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                                                      | Description                                                                                   | Default    |
|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| claims   | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | The claims to store. Coordinates are pulled from each claim's ``start_anchor``.               | _required_ |
| metadata | [MatchMetadata](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchMetadata`) \| None     | Explicit field-level provenance. When provided it overrides any per-claim metadata inference. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If any claim is non-synchronous (NOMATCH) or lacks a start anchor. |

### from_columns { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.from_columns }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.from_columns(
    timeline_a_ids,
    timeline_b_ids,
    coordinate_a,
    coordinate_b,
    *,
    unit_a,
    unit_b,
    metadata=None,
)
```

Build a field directly from parallel columns (the vectorized path).

This is the constructor a bulk producer (e.g. an alignment loader)
uses. It assembles the derived ``MatchClaim`` struct column straight
from the parallel inputs with :meth:`pyarrow.StructArray.from_arrays`
and **never** materialises a single :class:`MatchClaim` Python object,
so it scales to millions of rows.

Each row is a synchronous instant claim: ``timeline_a_id`` /
``timeline_b_id`` and the ``start_anchor`` sub-struct are filled from
the inputs; ``is_synchronous`` and ``is_explicit`` are ``True``;
``end_anchor`` / event ids / names / ``source_coordinate`` /
``metadata`` / ``source_claim_id`` / ``id`` are left null (the shared
metadata is injected on read, the id is generated on materialise).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name           | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Description                                     | Default    |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_a_ids | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                                                         | Timeline-A ids, one per claim.                  | _required_ |
| timeline_b_ids | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`)                                                         | Timeline-B ids, one per claim.                  | _required_ |
| coordinate_a   | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`) | Coordinate value on timeline A, one per claim.  | _required_ |
| coordinate_b   | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`) \| [float](`float`) \| [Fraction](`fractions.Fraction`)\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Array](`pyarrow.Array`) \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[ChunkedArray](`pyarrow.ChunkedArray`) | Coordinate value on timeline B, one per claim.  | _required_ |
| unit_a         | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                                              | Unit applied to every coordinate on timeline A. | _required_ |
| unit_b         | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                                              | Unit applied to every coordinate on timeline B. | _required_ |
| metadata       | [MatchMetadata](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchMetadata`) \| None                                                                                                                                                | Shared provenance for every claim in the field. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                | Description                     |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------------|
|        | \'MatchClaimField\' | A new :class:`MatchClaimField`. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the four inputs do not all have the same length. |

### max_coordinate { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.max_coordinate }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.max_coordinate(timeline_id)
```

The largest coordinate this field carries for ``timeline_id``.

Both anchor sides are scanned vectorized with :func:`pyarrow.compute.max`;
no claim is materialised.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description              | Default    |
|-------------|--------------|--------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) | The timeline to look up. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description                                                |
|--------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [float](`float`) \| None | The maximum coordinate value carried for that timeline, or |
|        | [float](`float`) \| None | ``None`` if the timeline does not appear in this field.    |

### to_claims { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.to_claims }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.to_claims()
```

Materialise every row into a list of :class:`MatchClaim` objects.

This is ``O(n)`` and defeats the columnar purpose for large sets; it
is provided for convenience and round-tripping, not for hot paths.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                      | Description                                |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[MatchClaim](`timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaim`)\] | A list of synchronous claims, one per row. |

### to_dict { #timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.to_dict }

```python
alignment.MatchClaimField.to_dict()
```

Serialize to a plain dictionary (inverse of :meth:`from_dict`).

The id and coordinate columns are emitted as plain Python lists (read
directly from the struct sub-fields); the metadata is emitted via
:meth:`MatchMetadata.to_dict` (or ``None``).

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A round-trippable mapping. |
